subject: Urgent: production 5xx/429 spike & timeouts — immediate mitigation required
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@ops.sable.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: production timeouts + 5xx spike — live customers affected

Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and client-side timeouts from our integration at 09:05 PDT. Error rate rose from ~0.3% to ~12% over 20 minutes. Customers are reporting long tail latency and intermittent 429s. We've attached a short trace and client error logs (sable-5xx-trace-20260822.log).

Current impact: several production jobs failing, web UI showing degraded completions. Can you confirm this is on your side and whether there's an immediate mitigation (rate-limits, alternate endpoint)? We're on a Dedicated pool with you (account DL-4473).

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform, Sable Labs

Attachment: sable-5xx-trace-20260822.log (text/log)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Mercer <alex@ops.sable.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production timeouts + 5xx spike — live customers affected

Alex — thank you for the heads up and the logs. We’re escalating immediately. I’m looping in SRE (Stephanie) and Ops (Lauren) to triage. Initial ask: please keep traces coming and note exact client request IDs for anything still failing.

Short-term we can:
- apply a short client-side rate cap and stronger retry-backoff (recommended 200ms jittered backoff)
- failover to a smaller quantized model variant if you want (will change latency/quality tradeoffs)
- open a provisioning request to add immediate capacity to your dedicated pool

We’ll confirm next steps within 30 minutes. I’ll also open an internal SR and mark this P1.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0113

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: RE: production timeouts + 5xx spike — diagnostics

Preliminary findings from SRE side (observed 09:00-09:30 PDT):
- Short window of 5xx/429 burst originating from Sable's dedicated pool in us-west-2.
- Autoscaler observed sustained queueing; new node provisioning lagged (~8-13 minutes) due to GPU allocation churn (spot reclaim + driver seating).
- Several pods entered crash-loop on NV driver mismatch; also observed aggressive client retries that amplified queueing.
- Error signature: 5xx with "runtime::gpu_unavailable" and 429s from token-queueing logic.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:28 PDT:
- Enabled emergency soft-rate-limit for Sable (20% below current peak) to arrest retry amplification.
- Provisioning request SR-8791 filed to add two reserved GPU instances (non-spot) into Sable's Dedicated pool — ETA 3 hours for warm-up, but we pushed for priority.
- Deployed temporary route to fallback model variant (rw-medium-8q) for non-critical routes to reduce memory/KV pressure.

Notes/asks:
- Finance/CS should confirm the dedicated pool quota bump authorization so we can convert the two nodes to reserved and avoid future spot churn.
- Sable: implement recommended client-side exponential backoff with jitter (we suggested 200ms -> 2s).

I’ll post more metrics once the reserved nodes come online.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: production timeouts + 5xx spike — exec note + next steps

Team — thanks for moving quickly. Two immediate asks for exec visibility:
1) Marissa — please send Sable an apology + mitigation note and include an offer for a credit for the downtime window.
2) Lauren — can you coordinate with capacity purchasing and finance to approve converting the two SR-8791 nodes to reserved (monthly commit) so they don’t ship on spot? This is a customer-critical account (DL-4473).

We should prepare a short exec summary for our VP and the Sable exec sponsor: timeline, root cause hypothesis (autoscaler + spot churn + client retry amplification), mitigations, and next steps (capacity reservation + postmortem).

I’ll be on the bridge if needed.
—Markus Klein
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Mercer <alex@ops.sable.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: production timeouts + 5xx spike — immediate mitigations applied

Alex — sincerely sorry for the disruption. Quick summary of what we did and next steps: 
- Mitigations executed: emergency soft-rate-limit, temporary fallback to rw-medium-8q for non-critical traffic, and prioritized provisioning (SR-8791).
- Recommended actions for Sable: implement exponential backoff with jitter and temporarily reduce client concurrency by ~25% for the next 6 hours. Stephanie included the exact backoff parameters above.
- We’ve initiated capacity conversion to two reserved nodes; Ops expects them to be ready in the next ~3 hours. I’ll confirm when green.

As a gesture we’ll apply a pro-rated credit for the affected window and schedule a joint postmortem with SRE / product / platform next week. I attached a short mutual action plan (sable-maf-aug22.pdf) with dates for follow-up.

Can we schedule a 30-minute bridge at 13:30 PDT today to review?

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: sable-maf-aug22.pdf (application/pdf)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, Alex Mercer <alex@ops.sable.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: RE: production timeouts + 5xx spike — status update and closure

Update (final): the two reserved GPUs were converted and attached to Sable's dedicated pool at 13:10 PDT on 2026-08-23. Error rate fell back to baseline by 13:35; no additional 5xx spikes observed. Root cause: a confluence of spot preemption events (driver driver/node churn), autoscaler cooldown/threshold tuning that delayed replacement for high tail workloads, and client retry amplification.

Follow-ups booked:
- Postmortem meeting: 2026-08-26 10:00 PDT (invite sent)
- Action items: autoscaler tuning (reduce provisioning cooldown in critical pools), offer reserved-node recommendation in onboarding docs, and add a retry advisory to the API docs.

Marking the incident resolved for now. I’ll attach the full collector logs to SR-8791.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
